Am I charged for missed calls, wrong numbers, or hang-ups?
No. You pay only for conversations your AI Employee actually handles. Spam, immediate hang-ups, and calls that never connect don’t count toward your usage.
What’s the difference between AI Receptionist and Enterprise?

AI Receptionist is built for single-location businesses running standard inbound flows — answering, booking, qualification, and follow-up. Enterprise adds outbound calling, complex routing workflows, multi-location management, white-label with custom URL, Director Mode for orchestrating multiple AI Employees, custom reporting, and our 200+ integrations including custom application connectors. If you operate more than one location or need to staff outbound calling, you’re an Enterprise customer.
How does pricing work across multiple locations?

Enterprise plans are priced at the organization level, not per location. One contract covers every location, with centralized control over scripts, voices, and integrations — and local flexibility for each site’s hours, services, and routing rules. Volume discounts kick in as your aggregate usage grows.
How long does deployment actually take?

A standard AI Employee deploys in three minutes from sign-up to first answered call. Enterprise deployments with custom integrations, multi-location rollouts, and white-label configuration typically run two to four weeks, depending on scope. Our team handles the buildout — you don’t need engineering resources.
What happens if my AI Employee can’t handle a call?

It transfers. You define the rules — escalate to a specific team member, route to an on-call number, send an SMS summary, or hand off mid-conversation with full context already collected. The AI Employee doesn’t get stuck or hang up; it knows when to bring in a human, and it briefs them before it does.
Do you offer custom contracts, SLAs, or Business Associate Agreement (BAA)?

Yes. Enterprise contracts include uptime SLAs, dedicated support, custom data processing terms, and BAAs for healthcare deployments. If you have specific procurement, security, or compliance requirements, our sales team handles them in the contracting phase.
How is this worth it compared to hiring a receptionist or using a call center?

A receptionist averages $40,000 a year, works one shift, and answers one call at a time. A traditional call center reads from a script and bills per-minute with markup. An AI Employee on Newo answers every call simultaneously, works every shift, books appointments directly into your calendar, updates your CRM, follows up on missed opportunities, and costs a fraction of either alternative. Most enterprise customers reach payback inside the first month — often on a single saved appointment.
